title: 12 Best Street Food in Oaxaca (2026)
description: The best street food in Oaxaca City, Mexico — curated from Reddit reviews, Eater, and BBC Travel. Tlayudas, memelas, empanadas, tacos, and nieves from legendary stalls and markets.

places.name: Mercado 20 de Noviembre

redditQuotes.text: One of the main reasons people come to Oaxaca is to eat, and I think they should visit the market.
The charcoal grills in Mercado 20 de Noviembre are an amazing experience.
redditQuotes.source: — BBC Travel · Chef's guide to Oaxaca

places.verdict: The beating heart of Oaxacan food culture. The Pasillo de Humo (Smoke Alley) is a sensory overload — vendors grilling tasajo, chorizo, and cecina over open charcoal. You pick your protein, they grill it, and a neighboring stall provides tortillas, salsa, and sides.

comparison.best for: First-time visitors — the ultimate Oaxacan food immersion
comparison.strengths: 4.5★ · Open daily 7 AM–7 PM · Dozens of stalls · Chapulines, chocolate, mole
comparison.limitations: Can be overwhelming; some stalls more tourist-oriented
comparison.what to order: Tasajo grilled to order in Smoke Alley. Add chapulines with lime and chile. Wash down with chocolate de agua.

places.whatToOrder: Tasajo grilled to order in Smoke Alley. Add chapulines with lime and chile. Wash down with chocolate de agua.

places.name: Tlayudas La Chinita
places.address: C. de Nuño del Mercado 209, Centro

redditQuotes.text: La Chinita not just for the tlayudas but for the street food experience.
Make the trek to Tlayudas La Chinita. It's a streetside show of grilling flair.
redditQuotes.source: — Eater · Street Food Guide to Oaxaca City

places.verdict: The most famous tlayuda stall in Oaxaca, featured on Netflix's Street Food. A late-night institution where a team chars chorizo, coaxes tasajo to perfection, and flips massive moon-shaped tortillas over charcoal.

comparison.best for: Late-night tlayudas after a mezcal crawl
comparison.strengths: 4.5★ · Netflix featured · Open until 12:30 AM · Organized numbering system
comparison.what to order: Tlayuda de tasajo — crispy tortilla with asiento, bean paste, cabbage, cheese, and grilled dried beef.

places.whatToOrder: Tlayuda de tasajo — crispy tortilla with asiento, bean paste, cabbage, cheese, and grilled dried beef.

places.name: Tacos del Carmen

redditQuotes.text: I recommend the tacos de chile relleno with chorizo and quesillo. So rich and delicious — the best in town.

places.verdict: Operating since 1977. Chef Alejandro Ruiz endorses the tacos de chile relleno — stuffed peppers rolled in tortillas that are spicy, meaty, and tender. A block from Santo Domingo Church.

comparison.best for: Afternoon taco fix near Santo Domingo
comparison.strengths: 4.6★ · Chef-endorsed · Since 1977 · English menu · Great agua de jamaica
comparison.limitations: Closed Wed & Sun; closes 2:30 PM; cash only
comparison.what to order: Tacos de chile relleno with chorizo and quesillo. Also try flor de calabaza. Wash down with agua de jamaica.

places.whatToOrder: Tacos de chile relleno with chorizo and quesillo. Also try flor de calabaza. Wash down with agua de jamaica.

places.name: Empanadas del Carmen

redditQuotes.text: They're made right in front of you, and they are the best in town — cheap and delicious.
Empanadas del Carmen makes damn good empanadas. Easily the best empanada de amarillo we had in Oaxaca.

places.verdict: Evening counterpart to Tacos del Carmen next door. Specializes in empanadas de amarillo — large corn tortillas folded around yellow mole, shredded chicken, and hoja santa. Chef Ruiz: 'cheap and delicious.'

comparison.strengths: 4.5★ · Netflix featured · Chef-endorsed · Made fresh · Open until 11 PM
comparison.what to order: Empanada de amarillo is the must-try. Also: quesadilla de flor de calabaza and quesadilla de champiñones.

places.whatToOrder: Empanada de amarillo is the must-try. Also: quesadilla de flor de calabaza and quesadilla de champiñones.

places.name: Memelas Doña Vale

redditQuotes.text: Doña Vale only makes memelas. Five options, no more. I love these kinds of places.

places.verdict: Doña Vale has been grilling memelas for 40 years. Chef Ruiz's #1 pick: 'Five options, no more. I love these kinds of places.'

comparison.best for: Breakfast memelas in a working-class market
comparison.strengths: 4.4★ · 40 years running · Chef's #1 memela · 5 items only
comparison.limitations: Closed Sundays; closes noon; outside tourist center
comparison.what to order: Memelas with tasajo grilled on charcoal, topped with eggs. Drink chocolate de agua or café de olla.

places.whatToOrder: Memelas with tasajo grilled on charcoal, topped with eggs. Drink chocolate de agua or café de olla.

places.name: Las Tlayudas de Mina y Bustamante
places.address: C. de Carlos María Bustamante 322, Centro

redditQuotes.text: From the moment I arrived in Oaxaca, this is where locals directed me for the best tlayudas in town.

places.verdict: Where locals send you for the best tlayudas. Off the beaten trail beyond the Zócalo, you'll smell the charcoal before you see it. Portions are enormous.

comparison.strengths: 4.4★ · Locals' pick · Open until 1 AM · Huge portions
comparison.limitations: Closed Wednesdays; cash only; limited seating
comparison.what to order: Tlayuda de tasajo or chorizo. Come hungry — portions are meant for two but you'll eat it all.

places.whatToOrder: Tlayuda de tasajo or chorizo. Come hungry — portions are meant for two but you'll eat it all.

places.name: Memelas San Agustín
places.address: C. de Manuel Fernández Fiallo 309, Centro

redditQuotes.text: Their memelas de salpicón pulled in a crowd on the daily. These ladies clearly have a passion for what they do.

places.verdict: A roadside stall with incredible variety — chicken tinga, chicharrón, pico de gallo, salpicón. The señoras clearly have a passion for what they do.

comparison.best for: Breakfast or lunch memelas with creative toppings
comparison.strengths: 4.5★ · Wide topping variety · Authentic roadside vibe · Cheap
comparison.what to order: Memelas de salpicón or chicken tinga. Try a trio with different toppings.

places.whatToOrder: Memelas de salpicón or chicken tinga. Try a trio with different toppings.

places.name: Tortas La Hormiga
places.address: Valentín Gómez Farias S/N, Centro (Jardín Conzatti)

redditQuotes.text: Tortas La Hormiga usually has quite the line. Locals line up for their combinados by morning.
The plaza that hosts the food truck is a great place to sit on a fountain's edge and munch your torta.
redditQuotes.source: — Eater · Street Food Guide to Oaxaca

places.verdict: A Oaxacan institution in picturesque Jardín Conzatti park. The line is always long but moves fast. Tortas are grilled panini-style on puffy white bread with quesillo, pickled veggies, and your choice of filling.

comparison.best for: Lunch in the park — Oaxaca's best tortas
comparison.strengths: 4.1★ · Iconic location · Fast turnover · Great park seating
comparison.limitations: Can sell out by early afternoon; limited menu
comparison.what to order: Torta de chile relleno or milanesa de pollo. All come with quesillo, salsa, pickled vegetables, and bean paste.

places.whatToOrder: Torta de chile relleno or milanesa de pollo. All come with quesillo, salsa, pickled vegetables, and bean paste.

places.name: Mercado Benito Juárez

redditQuotes.text: The kaleidoscope of tropical fruit, barrels of fried grasshoppers called chapulines, stands offering tacos and tlayudas.

places.verdict: The other essential Oaxacan market, right next to Mercado 20 de Noviembre. More focused on shopping (chapulines, chocolate, mole paste, quesillo, mezcal) but with excellent food stalls too. The cheese vendors alone are worth the trip.

comparison.best for: Stocking up on Oaxacan ingredients + quick market bites
comparison.strengths: 4.5★ · 32,500+ reviews · Central location · Shopping + food · Chapulines
comparison.limitations: Closed weekends; more shopping-focused than 20 de Noviembre
comparison.what to order: Bag of chapulines (fried grasshoppers), chunk of quesillo, and a cup of hot chocolate. Find a fonda inside for a mole plate.

places.whatToOrder: Bag of chapulines (fried grasshoppers), chunk of quesillo, and a cup of hot chocolate. Find a fonda inside for a mole plate.

places.name: Fonda Rosita
places.address: Av. José María Morelos 1522A, Centro (Mercado La Merced)

redditQuotes.text: Order the chilaquiles verdes. They come sizzling in a clay pot, with two fried eggs, onions, and crema on top. Ideal for post-mezcal haze.
redditQuotes.source: — Eater · Street Food Guide to Oaxaca

places.verdict: A market fonda inside La Merced market. The chilaquiles verdes come sizzling in a clay pot with fried eggs, onions, and crema. The ideal post-mezcal breakfast — Eater calls it the place where 'the day should begin.'

comparison.best for: Market breakfast — the best chilaquiles in Oaxaca
comparison.strengths: 4.3★ · Clay pot chilaquiles · Inside working market · Affordable
comparison.limitations: Can get busy at peak breakfast hours
comparison.what to order: Chilaquiles verdes — they come sizzling with fried eggs, onions, and crema. The tanginess of the tomatillo salsa is the ideal complement.

places.whatToOrder: Chilaquiles verdes — they come sizzling with fried eggs, onions, and crema. The tanginess of the tomatillo salsa is the ideal complement.

places.name: Nieves El Moy

redditQuotes.text: I was offered a sample of their maracuyá flavor infused with mezcal. I will definitely be going for that one next time!

places.verdict: A surprise discovery for many visitors. The leche quemada con tuna (burnt milk with cactus fruit) combo is Oaxaca's signature flavor. They also serve maracuyá (passion fruit) infused with mezcal — dangerously good.

comparison.strengths: 4.4★ · Signature leche quemada con tuna · Mezcal-infused options · Colorful stand
comparison.what to order: Leche quemada con tuna — Oaxaca's signature flavor. If available, try the maracuyá con mezcal.

places.whatToOrder: Leche quemada con tuna — Oaxaca's signature flavor. If available, try the maracuyá con mezcal.

places.name: Tlayudas Doña Tere
places.address: Escuela Naval Militar esq. Dallas, Col. Reforma

redditQuotes.text: The way she makes it is on charcoal, between the comal and the charcoal, so it's crispy and the cheese gets melted immediately. I love it.

places.verdict: Chef Ruiz's personal favorite for tlayudas: 'The way she makes it is on charcoal, between the comal and the charcoal, so it's crispy and the cheese melts immediately. I love it.' A 10-minute drive from downtown in a quiet residential area — the perfect escape from tourist crowds.

comparison.best for: Chef's secret — tlayudas away from the tourist center
comparison.strengths: 4.4★ · Chef Ruiz's personal favorite · Charcoal method · Quiet neighborhood
comparison.limitations: Outside tourist center; easy to miss; limited reviews online
comparison.what to order: Just get the tlayuda — charcoal-grilled, crispy, with perfectly melted cheese. Simple and perfect.

places.whatToOrder: Just get the tlayuda — charcoal-grilled, crispy, with perfectly melted cheese. Simple and perfect.
